newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore opposition party retains leadership.
newsitem.headline: Singapore opposition party retains leadership.

text.p: Members of a key Singapore opposition party voted to retain its current executive committee despite recent media speculation of a leadership challenge, a party statement said on Sunday.

The Singapore Democratic Party (SDP) said all 12 central executive committee members, including secretary-general Chee Soon Juan and chairman Ling How Doong, had been elected without contest at a closed-door meeting late on Saturday.
Singapore newspapers last week reported the possibility of a leadership challenge after the SDP's poor showing in the January 2 general election.
The SDP went from three parliamentary seats to none in the election, which saw total opposition seats fall from four to two. The governing People's Action Party (PAP) took 81 seats.

The statement said the SDP remained undaunted by its electoral defeat and would "continue to educate Singaporeans on the importance of democracy, to speak up for fellow citizens and to hold the PAP government accountable to the people."
